cross_source_reconciliation.path_lookup_result: writer/sandbox/executor.py was not present at the frozen-head path; repository code search did not surface writer/sandbox. Treat as Drive-only/later-uncommitted lineage until history-aware reconciliation proves ancestry.
cross_source_reconciliation.rule: Do not back-project this executor into the frozen PF head architecture.

executed_reproduction.probe: Read non-secret HOME presence, read /etc/hostname, write a benign marker to /tmp outside the per-execution cwd, then remove marker from the outer test harness.
executed_reproduction.interpretation: The documented temp-dir isolation is cwd isolation only; it is not a filesystem security boundary. Parent environment is inherited.

safety_findings.evidence: SandboxExecutor stores allow_network from config but executor.py contains no enforcement path for it. Processes inherit the host network namespace.
safety_findings.effect: Code believed to be network-disabled is not actually network-isolated.
safety_findings.required_contract: Network capability must be enforced outside generated code using a fail-closed namespace/seccomp/proxy capability boundary; a boolean carried only in Python state is insufficient.

safety_findings.evidence: Subprocess cwd is a fresh temp directory, but there is no mount/user namespace, chroot, Landlock/seccomp filesystem policy or path broker. Executed benign probe read /etc/hostname and wrote /tmp/frank_writer_escape_probe.txt outside cwd.
safety_findings.effect: Generated code can read/write any host path available to the Frank OS user, including project/state files, regardless of the sandbox temp directory.
safety_findings.required_contract: ClayCode execution must expose explicit capability-mounted inputs/outputs only; host filesystem is deny-by-default and destructive primitives cannot be reachable through ambient POSIX access.

safety_findings.evidence: env = dict(os.environ) passes the full parent environment to generated code. Benign reproduction confirmed inherited HOME visibility.
safety_findings.effect: API tokens, credentials or authority-bearing environment variables present in the parent may become readable by generated code.
safety_findings.required_contract: Start from a minimal allowlisted environment; secrets are never ambient and must be capability-brokered per operation.

safety_findings.evidence: ulimit -v and -u plus wall timeout are set, but stdout/stderr are fully buffered by parent communicate(), and no file-size/quota limit is applied to the temp directory or other writable paths.
safety_findings.effect: A child can consume parent memory through huge pipe output or disk through large writes despite its virtual-memory/process limits.
safety_findings.required_contract: Bound stdout/stderr bytes, writable storage quota, CPU time, wall time, open files and process count with externally enforced kill/cleanup semantics.

safety_findings.evidence: rust maps to rustc and the generic command is ['rustc', code.rs]; unlike Go there is no subsequent execution of the compiled binary.
safety_findings.effect: A Rust program can be reported successful when only compilation succeeded, making language-differential Harness results incomparable.
safety_findings.required_contract: Language adapters must implement compile+run semantics explicitly and declare execution surface/version.

safety_findings.evidence: cancel() sets _cancel_requested=True and it is reset only by cleanup(), not at the start/end of each execute call.
safety_findings.effect: A reused executor after one cancellation may label later successful executions Cancelled until cleanup is invoked.
safety_findings.required_contract: Cancellation state is per-execution identity, not shared sticky mutable state.

positive_controls: Uses a fresh temp cwd per execution and tracks cleanup directories.
Starts a separate process session and kills the process group on timeout/cancel.
Applies virtual-memory and process-count ulimits on Linux.
Uses non-interactive matplotlib backend and captures a bounded semantic output filename for plots.
Unsupported language is rejected before execution.

claycode: This executor is a historical precursor, not an acceptable security boundary. ClayCode must compile effect capabilities so destructive/network/host-filesystem actions are unrepresentable without explicit privileged capability tokens.
Separate pure computation runtime from effect broker; normal generated programs get no ambient POSIX host authority.
needle: Needle owns effect mediation; shell/process execution cannot bypass typed permission/effect checks by inheriting host user authority.
harness: Promote filesystem escape, env-secret exposure, network-deny enforcement, fork/output/disk bombs, timeout/cancel reuse and compile-vs-run language parity to mandatory adversarial tests.
unifieddb: Execution inputs/results/artifacts need provenance and bounded output storage; generated code must not open database files directly via host paths.
claygraph: Record requested capability set, granted capabilities, sandbox runtime identity and observed effects per execution event.
frank: Frank may reason freely about code but execution authority is a separate substrate. A statement like allow_network=false must correspond to an externally verifiable enforcement state.
gwt: Broadcast requested/granted/denied effects and execution result separately; never present 'sandboxed' as a fact from configuration alone.
clay: One-module fusion must preserve a hard capability boundary at the OS/effect edge; dissolving modules must not dissolve isolation.
